reasons: Deviation call is correct: Section 12.b's TrueLink indemnity is limited to TrueLink's breach/non-performance and contains no IP infringement, violation-of-law, data-compromise or gross negligence/willful misconduct trigger, which the detection guidance expressly treats as a deviation even though a (broad) Customer indemnity exists in 12.a.

Redline is actionable and directionally right: it adds the four preferred-position triggers to 12.b (IP infringement of the Interface/Hosting/Support Services, TrueLink's violation of law, TrueLink-caused unauthorized access to Client Content/Credit Data, gross negligence/willful misconduct) and inserts a balanced notice/control/cooperation/no-adverse-settlement procedure, using the existing 'claim arising out of' sentence structure.

Deterministic flags are not disqualifying: the 'vendor indemnity for IP infringement present' regex misses a phrasing variant (the inserted limb plainly covers 'infringe or misappropriate any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret or other intellectual property right'), and the 0.779 changed-character ratio on p0075 reflects the unavoidable expansion of a single-trigger sentence fragment into an enumerated list.
Comment is accurate, in-house voice, cites the playbook position and offers the sanctioned fallback (customary exclusions plus procure/modify/replace/refund).

Minor follow-ups, not grounds to fail: the proposal does not actually narrow Customer's 12.a indemnity (notably limb (iii)'s 'without regard to any knowledge limitation' and limb (iv)'s product-liability sweep), which the preferred position contemplates, and the new subsection should be confirmed as the next available letter in Section 12 and that 'Hosting Services'/'Support Services'/'Client Proprietary Information' are defined terms in the agreement.
